correctness.rationale: Uniqueness of the maximum-volume ellipsoid implies invariance under O(d−1), including the reflection needed in d=2, so there is no restriction on the original competitors. With k=1−t, the slab gives b≤c≤1−b and the maximum side functional equals kc+√(a²+k²b²). For k>0 any optimum has c=b and the side constraint saturated, so a²=1−2kb. Maximizing b(1−2kb)^((d−1)/2) on the feasible interval gives the unique critical point 1/[(d+1)k] clipped at 1/2, proving the contact transition including equality. The zero-volume endpoint at t=0,b=1/2 cannot maximize; for k=0 the cylinder directly gives a=1,b=c=1/2. Integrating sections gives κ_(d−1)Σt^j/d. In the first regime the varying volume factor is 1/(1−t^d); in the second it is the reciprocal of Σt^(j−(d−1)/2), whose paired reciprocal powers strictly decrease toward t=1. Continuity at the common branch value makes the increase global. Affine transfer preserves containment, optimization and volume ratio.
residual_risks: The frozen comparison cites the truncated-cone enclosing result as §7, Theorem 7.1; in the inspected 2007 Güler–Gürtuna preprint it is instead §8, Theorem 8.1. The printed section numbering is not needed for the proof. The theorem is not a claim about frusta with unrelated sections.
